# Option A: sectors, attenuators and ports (generated by option_a_sectors.py)

No steering emulation: the TG radios point their own beams, so only the final plan is cabled (the pre-event TG links plus the bridges E2–W2, E1–N, W1–S). Programmable attenuators take links down: every path to CORE and HUB at t0, and each bridge stays off-beam until its sites engage.

## Sectors per node

| Node | Type | Sectors used | Before the event | Final (after recovery) | Polarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HUB | DN | 3 (E, W, S) | E → E1, E2; W → W1, W2; S → S | off (destroyed) | E odd, W even, S odd |
| CORE | DN | 1 (N) | N → N | off (destroyed) | N even |
| W1 | DN | 2 (E, S) | E → HUB | S → S | E odd, S odd |
| W2 | DN | 1 (E) | E → HUB | E → E2 | E odd |
| E1 | DN | 2 (N, W) | W → HUB | N → N | N even, W even |
| E2 | DN | 1 (W) | W → HUB | W → W2 | W even |
| S | CN | 1 (single) | single → HUB | single → W1 | single even |
| N | CN | 1 (single) | single → CORE | single → E1 | single odd |

Sectors in use: 10 on the 6 nodes (of 24 available) and 2 on the 2 terminals: 12 in all. 14 node sectors stay unused (disable them; terminate their ports if they are RF-port builds).

Chain per path: 20 dB pad on each sector port, a 2-way splitter where a port reaches two peers, 3 dB of jumpers (assumed), one programmable attenuator. Cut = 95 dB.

Sector ports reaching two peers (2-way splitter each): E2-W, HUB-E, HUB-W, N-single, S-single, W2-E.

V-band parts: 9 programmable attenuators, 6 splitters, 12 pads (one per used sector port), 24 cables (two per path, one per splitter).

## Microwave hops

| Hop | Chain | At rest | At t0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1–CORE | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | 95 dB: taken down |
| CORE–E1 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | 95 dB: taken down |
| W1–W2 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | unchanged (can be taken down for other islands) |
| E1–E2 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | unchanged (can be taken down for other islands) |

## Ethernet: site switches and what each port carries

**W1** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link W1–CORE
2. IP-50: microwave link W1–W2
3. TG DN: TG links E: HUB; S: S (bridge)
4. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
5. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**W2** (4 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link W2–W1
2. TG DN: TG links E: HUB, E2 (bridge)
3. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
4. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**CORE** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link CORE–W1
2. IP-50: microwave link CORE–E1
3. TG DN: TG links N: N
4. TG controller: Terragraph controller (lost at t0)
5. DPIR server: DPIR planner (lost at t0)

**HUB**: no switch. The TG node's port only takes PoE power; it carries the hub links over the air interface and must not be wired to anything else.

**E1** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link E1–CORE
2. IP-50: microwave link E1–E2
3. TG DN: TG links N: N (bridge); W: HUB
4. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
5. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**E2** (4 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link E2–E1
2. TG DN: TG links W: HUB, W2 (bridge)
3. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
4. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**S** (3 ports)

1. TG CN: TG links single: HUB, W1 (bridge)
2. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
3. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**N** (3 ports)

1. TG CN: TG links single: CORE, E1 (bridge)
2. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
3. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

Site switches: 7 (W1 5, W2 4, CORE 5, E1 5, E2 4, S 3, N 3 ports; 29 in all), plus one out-of-band management switch for the agent PCs' second NICs, the attenuator controllers, the PDUs and logging. One managed switch with a port-based VLAN per site also works, provided inter-VLAN routing stays off: the sites may only meet through the radio links.
